why: These blobs are evidence, so they are verified before they are parsed. A test that reads a fixture somebody edited takes its green light from a rewritten baseline rather than from a loader that still reads old state. Check version and sha256, fail closed on either.
provenance: REAL CAPTURES, read out of this machine's Chrome Local Storage leveldb (Profile 2) on Tue 1 Sep 2026, one per origin the webui has run on. Each file is the exact string localStorage held, as production wrote it with a compact JSON.stringify: no reformatting, no trailing newline, so the file is byte-identical to what the browser stored. Version 1 of this manifest listed a single hand-built blob that claimed to be a build-605d5827 capture and was not - it was pretty-printed at 624 bytes against 511 for the same object compact, and had never been taken off a running build. Codex found it on #701 and it is gone.
immutable: Never regenerate one of these to make a test pass. The whole point is that a blob written by an OLD build still loads. Add a new capture per release; never edit an existing one.

prefs-blob-capture-6e8bf3c9.json.note: OLDEST shape captured: 8 keys, written before auto_play_*, usb_* and last_playlist existed. The backward-compatibility case with teeth - a build that assumes any of those keys is present fails here.

prefs-blob-capture-ea3349c1.json.note: 10 keys: auto_play_enabled and auto_play_enforce_order present, auto_play_maximize_reach not yet. The intermediate shape, so the ladder is not merely oldest-to-newest.

prefs-blob-capture-28fe8192.json.note: 15 keys, the full current shape including usb_* and last_playlist. Carries auto_play_enabled=true, the value the Tue 1 Sep 2026 incident turned on.
